text:
emma (CS): BrightCart just opened an urgent ticket — their strict JSON ingest started failing after today's canary rollout. They say their parser errors with 'Unexpected token \uFEFF' at char 0.

vikram (eng-runtime): can you paste the raw HTTP response (headers + body) they received? Also which model/route did they hit? :eyes:

emma (CS): pasted from customer:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 15:22:10 GMT

\uFEFF{"order_id": "BC-12345", "items": [{"sku":"SKU1","qty":2}], "total": 49.99}
```
They call our hosted endpoint /v1/generate with model redwood/gpt-infer-7b-v2-canary. They started seeing this after the canary flip earlier today.

sasha (support): customer impact = blocking checkout for some merchants. Severity = P1 for BrightCart. Ticket CS-5421. They need a workaround ASAP.

vikram (eng-runtime): thanks. quick hypothesis: the response body contains a UTF-8 BOM (\uFEFF) prefixed to the JSON which breaks strict parsers. Not typical from our service. Can we repro locally by calling the same model/route and streaming?

emma (CS): i repro'd with their curl and got same. Repro steps provided by customer:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-infer-7b-v2-canary","input":"produce structured order JSON for order BC-12345"}' -v
```
Response body begins with BOM as pasted above.

lee (eng-ml): interesting. i haven't seen BOM output from model generations before. possibilities: 1) system prompt or output filter in the canary accidentally prepended a raw U+FEFF char; 2) streaming/chunk concat bug that inserts a hidden marker; 3) some middleware (gateway) added a prologue. i'll reproduce against the canary image and also run a token-level dump to see if a zero-width char is generated.

vikram (eng-runtime): immediate mitigation: we can sanitize responses at the gateway layer to strip any leading BOM or common prolog patterns (e.g., XML <?xml ...?> or BOM). i'll open a hotfix PR to trim leading \uFEFF from body bytes before forwarding. that will be a short patch. we should also add a regression test.

lee (eng-ml): agreed. i'll check model config diffs between canary and stable. if model/system prompt was updated to add any invisible chars (rare but possible), we'll revert. otherwise we'll keep patch + rollback plan.

emma (CS): BrightCart on call window 17:30-18:30 UTC; proposed action: hotfix gateway sanitize + postmortem and rollback the canary if we find the model change is root cause. BrightCart prefers we avoid rollback if we can patch quickly.

sasha (support): flagged to account team and PM. sending ETA to customer: ~2 hours. adding workaround for their engineers: strip BOM on ingest side (js example):
```
const body = await resp.text();
const clean = body.replace(/^\uFEFF/, '');
const json = JSON.parse(clean);
```

brightcart-prod-bot: BrightCart automated alert: 42 failures in last 5m, first seen 2026-03-17T15:18:03Z.

vikram (eng-runtime): PR opened: runtime/strip-leading-prologue (hotfix). will deploy to gateway-staging first and then prod if green. also adding logging to capture any future non-printable leading chars.

lee (eng-ml): root cause snapshot: diff shows small change in canary streaming buffer that added a zero-width non-breaking char during chunk join. if confirmed we'll revert that patch.

emma (CS): thank you — i'll keep BrightCart updated and close CS-5421 once sanitized response is in prod. :thumbsup:

sasha (support): marking followup action items: 1) hotfix deployed 2) regression test added 3) postmortem scheduled 4) customer communication drafted.

vikram (eng-runtime): last note: auditing other customers that use strict JSON validators (list from ledger) and notifying them proactively.
